chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, may God have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Thabit ibn Dinar, from the Master of the Worshippers Ali ibn al-Husayn, from the Master of the Martyrs al-Husayn ibn Ali, from the Master of the Successors, the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them all, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, said:
The Imams after me are twelve. The first of them is you, O Ali, and the last of them is the Qa'im, through whom God, exalted is His mention, will conquer the East and the West of the earth.

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful; exclusive title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: The Imams; divinely appointed leaders of the Muslim community after the Prophet
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qa'im (the Riser); the twelfth Imam who will rise to establish justice on earth
key_terms.سَيِّدِ الشُّهَدَاءِ: Master of the Martyrs; title of Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali
key_terms.سَيِّدِ الْعَابِدِينَ: Master of the Worshippers; title of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about the twelve Imams and the Qa'im according to the narration in al-Amali of al-Saduq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Amali of al-Saduq, the Prophet Muhammad (S) declares through a golden chain of three Imams (Ali Zayn al-Abidin, al-Husayn, and Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them all) that the Imams after him are twelve in number. He identifies Imam Ali as the first and the Qa'im (the Awaited Mahdi) as the last, who will conquer the entire earth from east to west. This hadith is significant for establishing the Twelver Shia doctrine of the twelve divinely appointed Imams and connecting the concept of the Mahdi to the Prophet's own words.
